subject: CFA with four factors: problem in covariance matrix (I think)

messages.author: a42b37008ff2f80f
messages.subject: CFA with four factors: problem in covariance matrix (I think)
parts:
Good evening,

I'm working on a 4-factor confirmatory item factor analysis with binary predictors. The model has simple structure, but all latent factors are correlated.  
Items 1-3 load onto factor 1; Items 4-6 load onto factor 2; Items 7-10 onto factor 3; Items 11-15 onto factor 4. 

The model compiles, but when I attempt to sample, Initialization between (-5,5) fails after 100 attempts. I changed the range of initial parameters to (-5,5) because it wasn't working in the default. 

My best guess is that the covariance matrix is misspecified, but I'm not quite sure. 

[593] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                              
[594] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."                                                                          
[595] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                        
[596] "Exception thrown at line 69: bernoulli_logit_log: Logit transformed probability parameter is nan, but must not be nan!"                
[597] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
[598] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."  

My model is attached, and the data file is also attached. Any insight into why this may be happening is much appreciated. Thank you, in advance. I apologize for my limited understanding. 

Best wishes,
Allison

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Re: CFA with four factors: problem in covariance matrix (I think)
parts:
With this type of parameterization, you need multi_normal_cholesky to use a cholesky factor of a covariance matrix, but you're feeding it a cholesky factor of a correlation matrix.
I think you need to transform the cholesky correlation matrix (L) to a cholesky covariance matrix, and you need to estimate the sigmas for each of the factors.

See page 328 of the manual.
